raw_response:
The incident is a domain violation: some customers carry numeric region codes ('01'–'04') instead of region names. The 2026-01-15 CRM note says migrated customers carry a region code, and raw_region_map lists the codes. The map is complete, with 4 codes mapping one-to-one to 4 names. The fix is to translate the codes in silver_customers with a left join to raw_region_map, falling back to upper(region) when there is no match.

Checks on the map:
- Codes are unique, so the join cannot duplicate rows.
- The codes are VARCHAR, so the leading zeros are preserved.
- raw_customers has 200 distinct customers, so the row count stays at 200.
- The region names in the map are already uppercase.
- No whitespace issues are visible.

The mapping is authoritative: it is provided by the source and its purpose is stated in the change notes. Nothing suggests ambiguity, so this is a fix.

The only step that needs changing is silver_customers. The gold tables are rebuilt from it downstream.

{"diagnosis": "Customers migrated to the new CRM carry numeric region codes (01-04) instead of names; raw_region_map provides the code-to-name mapping, but silver_customers did not apply it. This puts the codes in silver and splits gold_region_daily by code.", "decision": "fix", "confidence": 0.93, "pre_sql": [], "step_overrides": {"silver_customers": "CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE silver_customers AS SELECT c.customer_id, COALESCE(upper(m.region_name), upper(c.region)) AS region FROM raw_customers c LEFT JOIN raw_region_map m ON c.region = m.region_code"}}
